saved_paragraphs.saved_paragraph: C&C makes two kinds of work visible at once: forceful operative assignments and the cleaning, serving, maintenance, study and company through which its members want to live. The institutional problem is how those capacities become obligations to particular people. A mission, a maid outfit, pleasure in serving, reported internal delegation and a useful result each supply some evidence; none supplies all the others. The complete café sequence gives this distinction practical form. C&C undertakes a temporary civic request and Yuuka reports a successful financial result. Neru nevertheless rejects Yuuka's proposal to make café work permanent. A valuable contribution has occurred without extinguishing the contributors' right to distinguish one occupation from another. [G12:L52–78]

The strongest bounded account is therefore an institution whose work becomes answerable through allocation, recipient response and correction, rather than through an assumed identity of perfect maids or indispensable combatants. C&C can defend school resources, contribute to a rescue, enjoy a costume and do actual housework. Its initiatives also create damage, surprise a leader with an already reported commitment, misread a customer, pressure a companion or extend help beyond the recipient's request. These are different failures and achievements. They make governance a set of contested relations, including who is informed, who may decide, what was actually requested, who bears costs and which result is shown. [P1:L46–56; P2:L40–60; G12:L56–78; T01:L298–302]

Chosen work deserves a precise meaning here. Akane's attachment to being a maid, Karin's affection for C&C despite earlier disappointment, Asuna's spontaneous enjoyment of service and Toki's wish to be useful are affirmative evidence. They do not prove that every task, disguise, bodily demand or employer arrangement is chosen on the same terms. Neru's jacket preference and refusal of permanent café conversion are equally intrinsic to the occupational account. Quiet evidence enters because it reveals what people want and how they negotiate a role; it need not first produce danger, income or a major plot turn. [A01:L242–268; K01:L237–253; AS01:L335–341; T01:L230–238; N01:L222–258]

This package owns the institution's student/operative labor responsibility and its two literal named arguments below. The differentiated-company ensemble, the individual character monographs, Seminar's wider allocation problem and the directed relations among particular members retain their separate homes. The institution argument draws on those people's acts and desires without claiming that institutional completion completes their friendship or every individual life. It is a bounded literary synthesis, with ROOT receiving and canonical adoption pending. [C01:L315–368; C05:L1–356; C07:L1–30]

The main-story comparison begins with a real assignment rather than a generic reputation. In Pavane Chapter 1, C&C and the council defend seized property while the game club's coalition attempts to obtain Mirror. Alice is deliberately used as a detained decoy; Karin's fire, Akane's escape, Asuna's intervention and Yuuka's reserves complicate a clean account of either party's victory. C&C's position is not automatically illegitimate because the protagonists want the file, and the protagonists' creative need does not settle the means of intrusion. At the same time, later testing and damage prevent security duty from certifying every defender's action. [P1:L46–54]

The withdrawal and aftermath matter as much as combat. Neru reports that Rio withdrew the assignment, then commissions further inquiry independently. Alice's later floor shot, fear and reported harm precede Neru's stopping pursuit. Building damage is said to have been processed as a club-activity accident; that reported handling does not show all injuries, property loss or threatened sanctions repaired. A task can cease without resolving every consequence. This is the first institutional control on treating C&C's operational success or an administrative category as complete answerability. [P1:L50–56; P1:L89–95]

Pavane Chapter 2 changes the distribution of work. Rio uses Toki and AMAS to seize Alice under a high-confidence danger interpretation. The danger and Momoi's injuries are real; the leap to exclusive destruction, secrecy and exclusion remains contested. C&C participates in the coalition against that process alongside Seminar, Veritas, Engineering, Eimi, Himari and the game club. These are actual different authors of a response, not interchangeable instruments activated by Sensei. Their local gains coexist with lost communications, exhausted resources and Neru's grave symptoms. [P2:L28–44; P2:L58–62]

The elevator operation is especially important for occupational credit. A prior Momoi idea, Yuzu's attribution, Chihiro's hypothetical mechanics and hacking, and C&C's enactment collectively produce the local opportunity for Neru's victory. Rio attributes the work to Sensei alone; Akane corrects that account. The result shows why credit matters institutionally: a rescue made by several students should not be rewritten as proof that all student expertise is derivative of adult authority. Victory still does not establish Neru's healing, Alice's immediate recovery or safe operation of all systems. [P2:L44–50]

The ending retains changes without inflating them. Alice externally returns to speech and ordinary game study; Neru is reported discharged after hospitalization. Neru objects to Toki's party appearance, then grudgingly contextualizes her obedience. Toki is present, not formally reassigned or fully forgiven. Rio resigns, disappears and leaves an apology while Yuuka protests and Himari retains facility work. An institution capable of plural rescue thus continues with unresolved employment, injury, technical and accountability tails. Its successful opposition to one coercive order does not establish a permanent governance settlement. [P2:L54–77]

Final provides another actual collective response. The accepted contextual account distinguishes Toki's proposed one-life self-destruction framing from Rio's refusal of that framing and C&C's arrival to help her. This is meaningful support; it does not settle Toki's work placement or absolve Rio. The same account preserves ordinary tastes, rest, games, views, tokens, errors, refusals and unequal labor among the contributors. Their crisis availability is therefore a locally achieved response, not proof that each member should always be available for any institutional demand. [F00:L227–235]

The later event and private repertoires supply additional locally complete sequences without an invented global calendar. EVENT825 has an urgent assignment that leaves Toki behind, her later wanted peer connection and chosen fight as a friend, and Neru's actual praise and apology. The crown and interception have positive endings, while transfer, payment and lasting satisfaction remain unfinished. Those meanings may be compared with the main-story uncertain return; they cannot be inserted into one dated life sequence from event numbers, costumes or release order. [PW:L233–237; T01:L240–246]

The ordinary cleaning scene begins by allowing students outside C&C to ask what they are seeing. Their maid-service and special-force interpretations have different provenance. Akane hums and invites cleaning; Neru objects to spectacle; Karin distinguishes clearing people from cleaning, and Asuna enjoys the dust. The ensemble's damaged dialogue labels remain qualified, so a member's stable temperament is not used to repair every turn. What survives securely is a double practice: real cleaning and operative vocabulary can coexist. Calling all cleaning violence would erase actual pleasure and labor; calling the maid image harmless would erase damage and intimidation. [G12:L52–56; G12:L101–106]

Karin's retrospective self-account refuses the simple choice between loving and regretting C&C. She says she came from a Seminar information-protection role, grew weary of fighting, and initially expected household learning, tea, sweets and cute clothes. She also values C&C memories, companions and service to Millennium. The account is hers, not a certified complete employment biography, and her disappointment does not negate present attachment. Institutional belonging can be chosen while some work remains unwanted; neither an initial misunderstanding nor later affection settles every assignment. [K01:L235–245]

Asuna's café encounter makes the distinction unusually clear. Mistaken for an employee because of her outfit, she chooses to play along for fun; neither pay, a contract nor staff permission is established by that scene. She later stops pretend work and sits for dessert. The wanted service and wanted leisure are both positive outcomes. Mission completion is narrated after a target arrives, but that accident does not make all the earlier pleasure covert strategy or prove a lawful arrest. The institution cannot own every enjoyable act merely because an operative happens to perform it in recognizable clothing. [AS01:L335–341]

Toki's clothing claim has another direction. She presents bunny attire as normal C&C infiltration clothing and values a rare assignment resembling her seniors' work. That is a situated norm claim and desire for belonging, rather than an inspected universal regulation. Guests read her appearance as Sensei's imposition; Toki first reads their attention as possible mission exposure and later as praise for looking good. The adult's discomfort and her imperfect interpretation remain distinct. Her escort and reported mission success do not settle reputation, the target's fate, authorization or all recipients' feelings. [T01:L387–395]

Akane's service presentation is also an active practice with private limits. She refuses proposed replacement addresses in one bond context, while written café dialogue offers different possible addresses. Her chosen maid role is not invalidated by that contextual variation. Uniform sources show classmates noticing a wall, a coached attempt that partly fails, actual accepted leisure and Akane's chosen disclosure that she wants to become closer. They also retain her uncertainty about herself. The institutional reading needs this possibility of uncertainty inside skilled presentation; polished responsiveness is not evidence that every desire is transparent or fulfilled. [A01:L252–280; A01:L284–298]

Privacy and selective audience are occupational constraints, not interruptions of the real story. Karin asks for changing privacy, refuses measurement and performance requests, sets photo and touch conditions, and stops topics. Neru conditions clothing help and demands deletion without a shown deletion result. Toki keeps a true hobby and an end-of-world plan undisclosed. These acts prevent service knowledge from becoming institutional entitlement to a person's whole interior. The absence of public disclosure is positive evidence of a limit, not permission to replace it with a guessed secret. [K01:L249–267; N01:L230–250; T01:L338–340; T01:L469–471; T01:L554–556]

Yuuka's fiscal objection begins with actual presented repair evidence and a concrete concern about expensive precision machinery and resources. Akane acknowledges the spectacular conduct and promises improvement. Yuuka relies on C&C and asks for quieter cleaning, yet the sequence ends with another large invoice. Its amount and itemization are not printed as an inspected ledger. This gives institutional criticism a real object and an incomplete correction: willingness to improve is shown as a promise, while the ending resists treating that promise as fulfilled cost control. [G12:L56; G12:L84–89]

The next request is situated civic work. Merchants in the electronics district ask Seminar to take responsibility for a student-café festival. Yuuka initially questions its remit, then accepts a district obligation and asks C&C to run a polite maid café for one week. C&C's previous infiltration and costume experience make the proposal intelligible, but ability to wear the outfit does not supply willingness to perform this task. Karin's interpretation of the request and her correction of the register preserve communication as actual work. No statutory municipal charter or universal school duty is supplied by Yuuka's judgment. [G12:L60–64]

Neru learns of a reported prior commitment after an hour and explicitly refuses. Karin reports acceptance, budgeting, a signed contract and withdrawal costs; Asuna acknowledges signing; Akane states an internal rule by which Asuna could decide in the club head's absence. These are the exact evidentiary degrees: an acknowledgment, a report and a stated rule. The source does not display the signed instrument, authenticate its legal validity or show Neru's free prior assent. A pressure-producing commitment can be narratively real without an analyst certifying enforceability. The timing of her objection is part of the institution's information problem, rather than proof that leader status makes all earlier absence decisions illegitimate or all later participation willing. [G12:L66; G12:L110–120]

Asuna's interest in the unusual work and in a revenue share is likewise retained as her reason, not a universal club motive. Karin and Akane have their own curiosity and pleasure. Neru's resistance is not answered merely by pointing to those other members' enjoyment or to costs said to follow withdrawal. The club proceeds to an actual opening and a compressed week, with preparation disagreement and the appearance negotiation below still visible. Temporary enacted participation is a narrower result than enthusiastic conversion, informed prior delegation or endorsement of every term. [G12:L66–76]

After the explicit week, Yuuka reports earnings sufficient in her assessment to compensate damage and thanks the members. The report gives the work an actual retrospective institutional value; it is not a displayed payment transfer, itemized audit or complete restitution. Her next proposal changes its scale. Because café work is profitable, attractive and suitable in her view, she suggests abandoning agent work, maintaining maid work and servicing festivals as an exclusive Millennium resource. This proposal is not an enacted reorganization. Neru's silence and then direct refusal and threat terminate the attempted conversion in the printed exchange; no actual assault or permanent reassignment follows. [G12:L76–78; G12:L130–131]

This is the required chosen-occupation argument: fiscal value, capability and gratitude justify taking a contribution seriously, yet none alone determines the worker's future vocation. Neru's refusal is a decision about that proposed use of C&C, while the successful temporary work remains successful at its reported scope. Yuuka is neither merely an enemy of pleasure nor an impartial accountant whose favorable return settles the matter. She supplies resources, thanks and an expansionary proposal that its intended recipient rejects. Keeping all three directions makes answerability legible without needing Sensei to mediate the sequence; Sensei does not directly act in this GROUP account. [G12:L56–78; G12:L95–120; G12:L131]

GROUP3101 supplies a separate, consequential fiscal comparison. Akane seeks funding as an individual student, not on behalf of a C&C operation. She wants a more efficient innovative cleaning solution; Yuuka identifies the compressed-hot-gas proposal as a flamethrower and refuses it as an existing, non-new device. A disappointed ordinary maker's request remains evidence even when denied. The account does not show firing the device, a safety investigation or a club-wide funding application. Yuuka's claimed practical criteria and the report of limited resources are real local allocation arguments, not an evaluation of the analytical value of quiet desires. [G31:L90–102; G31:L152]

The later Himari case reveals revisability and risk in the same budget practice. Noa reports that Veritas is not formally recognized and Rio said not to fund Himari individually. Yuuka nevertheless supplies personal name and money for a proposed predictor; actual construction depends on Noa's labor, and a requested metal forecast yields a horoscope. The later financial windfall remains hedged rather than an inspected causal or accounting proof. These facts complicate a purely neutral utility rule without making every denied request right. They belong to Seminar's separate institutional home as well; this section uses them only to clarify C&C's individual-versus-club request and the difference between declared allocation criteria, personal discretion and achieved outcome. [G31:L108–138; G31:L152]

Akane's appearance initiative begins with her own enjoyment of the café presentation and Karin's admission of pleasure. Neru objects to relinquishing her sukajan jacket and says she may leave. Akane accepts that specific jacket boundary, then negotiates hair arrangement; Neru agrees to the hair. This is a completed local distinction inside one shared job: the recipient allows one change and refuses another. Neither the original reluctance nor the permitted hair should be flattened into total rejection or total consent. The club's capacity to work through differentiated terms is more informative than a claim that one standardized maid image binds every member. [G12:L70]

The jacket has an intrinsic private history of preference. Neru likes it because it looks good to her; the matching proposal remains unfulfilled. Its recognizability to others does not make its value merely a uniform code, and wearing other clothes does not replace her with a docile person. Her uniform repertoire explicitly rejects that interpretation, while choosing toys, food, a pond, rides and rest. These small wants belong inside the occupational argument because they make permanent visual conformity an inadequate account of what the wearer may choose. They do not need tactical benefit to matter. [N01:L222–250]

Akane's initiative is equally more than managerial enforcement. Her own sources give wanted visibility, fresh clothing, favorite tea, learning about bearing and a wish to show another side. Her self-reproach about being an inadequate maid is situated uncertainty, answered locally through praise and reassurance; it is not a rule that a desire beyond usefulness makes a worker unfit. Giving Neru control over one article does not erase Akane's pleasure in arranging an appearance. It preserves two active directions: making a presentation and choosing how to receive it. [A01:L264–278; G12:L70]

Asuna's play and Karin's personally enjoyed bunny attire cannot supply Neru's assent. Toki's norm claim about infiltration clothing cannot supply it either. Each is valuable evidence at the stated recipient and context, while Neru's own public-wearing choice in another private encounter remains another choice. Institutional standardization has to meet particular recipients, not add up other members' liking into a collective permission. This remains true when clothing is helpful operational equipment and when everyone is affectionate. [K01:L239–251; AS01:L277–283; T01:L389–395; N01:L230–262]

The café opening retains labor beyond appearance. Asuna recruits guests before Neru considers preparations complete; Karin slips from customer service into target-processing vocabulary, and Akane corrects the language. No harmed patrons are shown. These errors and interventions demonstrate that adopting a service image does not complete preparation or recipient-facing skill. The finite printed result is an opening, a reported successful week and a rejected permanent conversion, with the hair agreement and jacket refusal preserved rather than retrospectively overwritten by revenue. [G12:L72–78]

Karin's literal housekeeping and self-chosen apron join usefulness, cuteness and experimentation. She wants to do necessary work first, but service does not prove unlimited ability: the event shop says she cannot help with calculation, and academic effort has no printed passing retake. Her café ambition remains a wanted future rather than an achieved career. This makes ordinary desire institutionally informative without making it a productivity metric. A dream can orient present belonging while still being unfinished; an arithmetic limit does not disqualify her pleasure in another kind of work. [K01:L237–249; K01:L287–307]

The unnamed lunch friend's answer is an independent ordinary act. When Karin brings pizza, the friend brings salad, changing the relation from one person giving up a preference into adjustment by both. That friend remains unnamed; her actual response cannot be assigned to a known member for convenience. Karin's later self-chosen commute and refusal of a rail-slide demonstration likewise preserve enjoyment and a limit in one setting. These outcomes matter because the institution's members have peer relations and tastes beyond commands, public force and the adult's approval. [K01:L247–253; K01:L299–307]

Asuna can enjoy helping and misjudge a boundary in the same repertoire. At a laundrette she offers company and household assistance; some proposed work is unaccepted while shared time and sunrise return are actual. In the bread encounter there is a purchased meal, the adult pays, and the quantity overshoots her appetite. A service narrative that retained only enthusiasm would lose the unaccepted offer and excess; a failure-only narrative would lose the pleasure of ordinary company and food. Neither outcome is trivial because it has little bearing on a battle. [AS01:L235–241; AS01:L301–305]

Her phone search gives care a relation to fallibility. The phone is lost, communication is broken, the joint search finds it on a bench, and Asuna apologizes. She values the missed calls and saves the evidence as a treasure; her comparisons with other C&C members remain her appraisals rather than inspected accounts of their motives. The future promise not to lose it again is not a cure. Wanted connection is here organized around an actual breakdown and recovery, not an always-successful intuition or a requirement that a good operative never inconvenience anyone. [AS01:L323–329]

Akane's chosen early waking aims at conversation, but the adult sleeps again and the wanted conversation does not happen. Tea and a prepared welcome can support real rest without making a house shared property or fulfilling her wish to be the first person seen at every waking and return. A rare day off, wanted chance company and favorite tea supply desire beyond service. Actual accepted peer leisure later supplies a different outcome, while tentative loneliness and uncertain self-disclosure remain unresolved. The institution gains a fuller account of a worker by keeping both missed and achieved company. [A01:L260–280]

Neru's can challenge, jacket, toy, pond and rides are similarly valuable without a hidden training purpose. Failed kicks and mishaps coexist with repeated enjoyment. Her request for bedside company is a request, not permanent availability, and imagined nursing is not a separately achieved care act. The theme-park invitation's later permission to decline is a positive local revision; it does not retroactively repair every earlier threat or coercive request. Ordinary life makes differences between chosen amusement, proposed reciprocity and actual uptake especially visible. [N01:L222–262]

Toki's hobby question directly resists the rule that pleasure needs a useful output. Films, comics and shopping fail to supply an immediate satisfying pastime; she asks whether a hobby must yield something or mean something, then chooses to keep a possible answer private. Later reports of enjoyable games and comics and actual shared viewing can be compared at their local reference, without filling the earlier secret or imposing a costume-based growth ladder. Her warm bed, tea aroma, chips, wish for a room, provisional tastes and valued dawn are not preparatory data for a future crisis verdict. They are wanted life. [T01:L332–340; T01:L406–433; T01:L463–471; T01:L505–509; T01:L535–556]

Rest also has an explicit relation to labor. Toki says she is human and needs rest, can want to slack off as well as assist, and finds both endless idleness and emergency tension consequential. Her recipe, cleaning and prioritized task list are positive competent work; an emergency explanation does not justify interpreting every quieter day as incapacity or every performance claim as objective perfection. A bounded institution account can recognize real disciplined effort while declining the premise that gratitude makes exhaustion, constant connection or invasive care legitimate. [T01:L444–452; T01:L537–539; T01:L550–556]

C&C's main-story competence is substantial, and its attribution must remain distributed. Karin's fire, Akane's escape, Asuna's intervention and Neru's local victory matter at different points; Toki's correct deductions also coexist with a missed frontal approach and the disruption of her evasion. The coalition's ability to revise plans is a positive resource. None of these facts makes an operative's own report a complete technical account, removes another student's injury or converts a power ranking into a measured all-context capability. Institutions need contributors whose particular labor remains visible alongside its constraints. [P1:L48–54; P2:L40–50; P2:L68–75]
